Put context to work

What you can do with SSH and AI

Standardize incident checks

Use configured runbooks for service status, disk usage or bounded logs. AI selects a known check and supplies validated parameters instead of composing unrestricted shell text.

Review an operational change

When AI requests an existing maintenance runbook, the approval shows the fully rendered command, target host and parameters. Execution waits for your decision.

Reach private infrastructure

Use the network access already available on the GateRook computer, including its VPN and an optional SSH bastion. A Vault SSH CA can issue short-lived user certificates for calls.

From service to MCP

How to connect SSH

GateRook must be running on a computer that can reach your service. Open Connections, choose Add connection, and select SSH. Give the connection a name and environment.

New to GateRook? Start with the full setup guide.
  1. 01

    Add the SSH target

    Add an SSH connection named stage-vm in the stage environment. Enter the host, port and dedicated user. Choose a private key, password or Vault SSH CA credentials; Vault SSH CA requires an external Vault store configured in Secrets.

  2. 02

    Verify the host identity

    Run Test connection and compare the host fingerprint with your trusted record before accepting it. If you use a bastion, configure and verify its own user, credentials and host key as well.

  3. 03

    Choose an existing runbook

    In Connectors, open Templates and locate a configured SSH runbook whose Runs on connection is stage-vm. The desktop build currently has no runbook creation editor. The example below requires an existing uptime runbook with command uptime, reviewed and confirmed read-only; it is not created by adding an SSH connection.

  4. 04

    Keep the execution scope small

    Use Runbooks only and publish ssh_run on the endpoint. Existing runbooks expose their validated parameters to the AI client. Mutating runbooks wait for approval; arbitrary ssh_exec is a separate tool and is off by default. If the connection has no configured runbooks, ssh_run has nothing to execute.

  5. 05

    Choose the endpoint and tool modes

    Add the tested connection to an endpoint. In Tools & policies, enable only the tools needed for the task. Start with Read only where supported; use Approval for any selected mutation and leave other tools Off. A connection alone does not grant an AI client access.

  6. 06

    Connect your AI and verify the first call

    In Clients, choose your AI app and endpoint, review the connection details, and connect. Try this guide’s example in Playground before asking your AI. Open Activity to inspect the tool, target, decision and returned result. The getting started guide covers this shared flow.

Connection settings

Configure SSH in GateRook

These are example values for the connection form. Enter credentials into GateRook’s secret fields, not into an AI prompt. Requirements and alternatives are noted per field.

SSH connection configuration
SettingExampleHow to use it
Hoststage-vm.internalThe core connects from this computer, so its VPN, DNS and hosts file apply.
Port22Change this if the SSH server listens on another port.
Usergw-runbooksUse a dedicated account with the permissions needed by the saved commands.
Credentials methodprivateKeyEnter an OpenSSH or PEM key in the protected field. An optional passphrase and user certificate are supported.
Runbooks onlytrueRejects ssh_exec regardless of endpoint mode. This restriction defaults to true for prod connections.
Host keyConfirm during Test connectionVerify the displayed fingerprint against a trusted source, then pin it. Existing known_hosts lines can also be supplied.

Know what you expose

SSH tools and access boundaries

The connector determines what is possible. Endpoint modes and connection policies determine what a particular AI client may use.

Available tools and access behavior
ToolPurposeAccess behavior
ssh_runRun a saved runbook with its validated parameters. Reviewed read-only runbooks can run in Read only mode; runbooks that may change state require approval.Read only / Approval
ssh_execRun an arbitrary command only when the connection and policy permit it. Every such command is treated as a mutation and requires approval.Off by default

Before you enable access

  • The desktop build has no SSH runbook creation editor yet. A runbook must already be configured on the selected connection before AI can call it; the uptime example illustrates that prerequisite.
  • Read-only is a human-reviewed declaration for the command, not a remote operating-system sandbox. A changed command needs its read-only confirmation again.
  • ssh_exec is off by default, always requires approval when enabled, and is refused when Runbooks only is on.
  • The SSH account still determines the operating-system permissions. Command timeouts and output limits bound a call; they do not make a powerful account unprivileged.

GateRook stores local connection secrets encrypted and resolves them for connectors. Allowed tool results are returned to your AI client and may be processed by its provider. Scope the data you expose as well as the actions you allow.

Practical answers

SSH connection questions

Use Test connection to isolate service access problems. Use Playground and Activity to inspect endpoint permissions and tool calls.

Where do I create an SSH runbook?

The current desktop build does not provide a runbook editor. Connectors > Templates lists existing runbooks and their connection, but New template > SSH runbook is unavailable. This guide demonstrates a preconfigured runbook; a new SSH connection alone does not supply one.

Do I need to give my SSH key to the AI client?

No. Configure the key or credential source in GateRook. The MCP call names a connection and runbook; it does not contain the SSH private key.

Can I connect through a bastion?

Yes. Configure the optional jump host with its own user, credentials and host key. The bastion must permit TCP forwarding.

What happens when I change a read-only runbook?

Its read-only confirmation is tied to the exact command. A changed command waits for approval until you review and confirm it again.
